When you said "statistically" at the start of your post, I felt that it was disingenuous because you follow that up with some incredibly inaccurate statistics just to try and prove a point.

There's nothing that grinds my gears more than a disingenuous use of the word "statistically".

Not everyone in public matches wants to take the game seriously and that's fine. (Yes, it's actually fine regardless of your (or my) personal opinion on the matter)

So perhaps a scrimming and tournaments are more suited for you.
Considering the main problem you're facing here is a lack of competitive spirit from your comrads.

I hope I've been of some assistance to you :)

replies.author: Petlas
replies.body:
A'right, if any points in this post have already been brought it, it simply means that I've been too lazy to notice that they've already been mentioned. Same goes for any typos or shit that may not make sense. It's 8 in the morning, go cry about it.

The command has its benefits and disadvantages. A majority of the benefits revolve around people whose chat messages aren't directed to you in particular. I'll give a quick example: If a kid happens to come along and spam about how much lag they're getting every couple of seconds, you can /ignore them without any hassle. They won't try and get you to unignore them because frankly, they don't give a shit if you're getting their constant messages of 'lag' and 'omg block lag fix now' or not.

But, on a different note, if a kid (Yes, I'm going to keep referring to players as kids. Go cry about it) is continuously trying to provoke you (eg. calling you a noob over and over) and you /ignore them, you are only going to provoke the kid more than you are being provoked yourself. The kid may start seeking other ways to make contact with you as well as become agitated because he/she has been /ignore'd.

They could spam signs in front of you with what they're trying to say, continue to spam the chat without realising they've been /ignore'd, team grief to try and catch your attention and much more. A /report or two may even be involved. I recall some of these points being brought up a while ago when a /mute command was suggested to staff (Obviously I don't have access to the topic anymore, but there may be one or two current staffers who know what I'm referring to (: ) and it convinced the majority of us that /mute was a bad idea.

To sum it up, /ignore can be used with ease against players spamming with no particular target (or not you, at least), but if it's used against a player targeting you, the player could go to bigger extents to try and get your attention.

Oh, and regarding the team situation, it depends if players see the game as solo or team based themselves. The teamwork element can be used in several different ways, but it's more used for the defending aspect of the game. Defending a monument/skybridge/base almost entirely depends on teamwork, for example. For things like rushing to get a monument, these can obviously have teamwork involved as well, but it's more of a solo thing regardless of any teammates you may have around you.

replies.author: Petlas
replies.body:
"TNT griefing can't be done without any TNT maps." That's true, but in the unfortunate case of a provoked player during a TNT map match, it can happen.

"Team spleefing can't be done with a bedrock layer at the buttom." Can't be done at all? Almost, if not every map has a bedrock layer at the bottom, yet team spleefing is one of the most common forms of team griefing. Don't forget player-made bridges and platform extensions.

"Team griefing can be easily avoided and reported." It can't be as easily avoided if a certain player is determined as fuck to ruin your gameplay (eg. Constantly blocking you in, blocking your path, breaking crafting tables, ruining structures you make, etc.) But yes, it can be stopped if there's an available staff member standing by.
